title: im Stagnant!
author: Spare-Ad-1024
selftext: As I mentioned in a previous post, now with video evidence, this project have left me feeling stuck.  Any attempts to improve the game simply involve using quotas without making any real progress.

comments.author: SeasawPhilosopher
comments.body:
There’s a lot here so pick a small area you want to make look better instead of trying to tackle it all. Capture screens from several angles in that area. Send those images to Claude code or Codex and chat about what’s wrong. Gather a selection of reference screens from other games you want to try to get closer to the quality of and have the AI tell you where you’re lacking in terms of models, materials, lighting, etc. Then just start chipping away at things.

The boat is right in the wheel house (pun intended) of AI because it can gather references photos to model it from. So tell it to gather references photos and schematics if they exist, model the full thing, and find high quality PBR materials to texture it all with, and use material layering and shaders to add detail and wear. Fable 5.2 can excel at this, and Opus 5.5 isn’t far behind.

Don’t model the humans, you can use Unreal or Blender plugins a or something else for that, or even meshy or trip. LLMs aren’t great at that kind of modeling yet.

comments.author: kytheon
comments.body:
The walking animations look awful. Get a bunch of animations from Mixamo and tell your AI to use it.

Also your game lacks purpose. It's a tech demo but what's the point?

replies.author: Spare-Ad-1024
replies.body: The point is to make a RPG game where you walk about, talk to people, perform quests and in the end survive the sinking.

comments.author: Skubcraft
comments.body: Don't feel bad about working on the game under the hood. The stuff no one sees is often the most important.

comments.author: JessicaTian8
comments.body: I've been there. When I'm not a coder, it's easy to keep asking for big fixes and just burn usage. What helps is shrinking the ask: pick one small thing that feels wrong, describe exactly what you see and what you want instead, and stop once that one thing works. If a chat gets messy, starting fresh with a short summary of the project often works better than pushing on.
